title: Design of a low-emission long-range aircraft using UNICADO
abstract: Abstract In this paper, the UNICADO 2.0 software is used to simulate and evaluate measures regarding the reduction of energy consumption and climate impact of long-range aircraft. For this purpose, an Airbus A350-900-like reference aircraft powered by a Trent XWB-84-like aero engine is generated. The measures investigated are SAF, liquid hydrogen and a reduction in cruise speed. The design of a liquid hydrogen aircraft with cryogenic tanks hereby discloses significant challenges regarding landing gear integration, tail strike and competitive transport work. The combined implemented measures of liquid hydrogen and a reduced cruise speed lead to a maximum reduction, compared to the reference aircraft, in the climate impact of 82% in average temperature potential, 80% in absolute global warming potential and 76% in absolute global temperature potential; however, leading to an increase in fuel consumption of 13.6% due to the lower cruise Mach number. This and the necessary change to an economy-class-only layout over two passenger decks for the liquid hydrogen configuration show the at times inverse relation of climate impact reduction measures and economic feasibility. Furthermore, the scope of interest is shifted over the system boundaries of the aircraft. Thus, including hydrogen production in the environmental evaluation. Assuming a production in Germany in the year 2022, an increase in the $$\textrm{CO}_2$$ equivalent of 156% compared to the reference aircraft is obtained. However, when assuming energy production solely from wind turbines a reduction of 92% is possible.
problem: This paper addresses the challenge of reducing the climate impact of long-range aircraft by evaluating alternative fuels, which reveals significant aircraft design challenges and an inverse relationship between the effectiveness of climate impact reduction measures and their economic feasibility.
method: This paper uses UNICADO 2.0 software to simulate and evaluate the climate impact reduction of a long-range aircraft by designing and comparing configurations that utilize sustainable aviation fuel, liquid hydrogen, and reduced cruise speeds against a conventional reference aircraft model.
task: The task is to simulate and evaluate measures, including using sustainable aviation fuel, liquid hydrogen, and reducing cruise speed, to lower the energy consumption and climate impact of a long-range aircraft using the UNICADO 2.0 software.

innovation: This paper presents a comparative design study of a long-range aircraft, evaluating the climate impact, performance, and feasibility trade-offs of using sustainable aviation fuel, liquid hydrogen, and reduced cruise speeds as decarbonization strategies.

For the modelling of the liquid hydrogen engine (Trent LH2) in GasTurb 14, the original kerosene version of the Trent ILR is used with no variation in the polytropic efficiencies of compressor or turbine, as well as other parameters. To model the thermodynamic cycle characteristics of the Trent LH2, the energy carrier in GasTurb 14 is set to liquid hydrogen, implying an energy density of 118.429 MJ/kg. Calculations for the LTO cycle and cruise, approximated with 35,000 ft, show maximum deviations from the reference engine Trent ILR of 3%, 0.6% and 2% for the mass flow, temperature, and pressure, respectively. In the context of this publication, the deviations are seen as negligible. Hence, mass flow, temperature and pressure data from the reference aero engine are used for the SAF engine.
